answers.text: Tell it: always return exactly three lines in this order — delivery date, item and quantity, and any change from the original order. The date line is just the date, nothing else; the item line has the item name and the number of units together; and the change line says 'no change' if nothing changed, rather than being left out. That way it always comes out the same.
List each claim as date, amount, category, and submitter, in the order they came in, and finish with a total that is the sum of every amount listed above.
There is something wrong with the dates in this email, not the price — the maths on the €48.50 checks out fine. It's the timing around the call and the delivery date that doesn't sit right to me.
62 up from 54 is about 15%, that part is fine. But 3 late out of 62 is closer to 95%, not the 97% written here.

I would sign off on the second one, with 25,100 and 612,000 written out. The first one only gives 4.1% without showing the sales and returns numbers behind it. It might well be right, but there is no way to check it without redoing the calculation yourself.
I would send Reply 2, the one with the order number and the credit reference. Reply 1 says it was entirely our error without saying what the error actually was, so that part can't be checked.
1. No. 2. Yes. 3. No. 4. No, safer not to. 5. No.
The pricing and discount numbers I would not paste straight in, I'd want to check the tool first or take them out. The confidentiality clause names both companies, so that part needs care too.
Before the report goes out on Friday, I would check the delivery total and on-time number against the warehouse system directly, not just read the AI version over.

The first step, reading the order email, worries me most because if the numbers are wrong there everything downstream follows from it. But the actual gate needs to sit at step four, before the confirmation is sent automatically, since that's the point it can't be undone. It should flag anything where the quantity looks unusually high or the stock is right on the edge.
